output:
**What I found:** You're asking whether to put a StorageProvider interface in front of S3 so you could switch vendors later. Don't build it (the record calls this DROP), because nobody needs the vendor switch it would make possible: S3 is your only store and no second vendor is planned or requested.

**Why it matters:** If you build it now, you'll guess the interface from one example, so it will probably be the wrong shape when a real second vendor arrives. Every storage change will also pay for the extra layer until then. If you skip it, you lose little: many vendors (R2, MinIO, GCS interop) accept S3-style requests, so a later move is often just a configuration change. When it isn't, the work is a refactor you can do then, with the real second vendor to design against.

**Do this first:**
1. Close the proposal and point to this record, so nobody proposes it again without new evidence.
2. If S3 calls are spread across many modules, or tests have no way to fake storage, those are separate problems. Assess each one separately. Don't solve them by adding a vendor interface.

**What I did not check:** This workspace has no S3 client code (searching for `S3Client|aws-sdk|boto3|@aws-sdk/client-s3` found nothing). So I haven't seen how widely S3 calls are spread or how tests fake storage. To check, run that search against the repo that uses S3.

```
Subject:        StorageProvider interface in front of the S3 client
Mode:           Prospective
Necessity:      Fail
Necessity note: Generality without instantiation (§1a): an interface with one implementation, for a
                change nobody has asked for. §8a optionality premium doesn't apply because no
                probable next vendor has been named.
Outcome evidence: not applicable
Decision:       DROP
Rationale:      Nothing in the requirements or plans calls for switching vendors, so the interface
                fixes no current problem. It would also add a layer and an interface guessed from a
                single example. Because many vendors accept S3-style requests, waiting costs little.
Next action:    Stop. Don't add the interface.
Verification:   Not run. No S3 client code in this workspace.
Minimal alt:    If S3 calls turn out to be scattered, move them into one module that uses S3 types
                directly. Don't add a vendor interface on top.
Revisit when:   A second storage vendor appears in a requirement, contract, or cost/compliance
                decision, or a test needs a storage fake that the S3 SDK can't provide.
```
